- **This is the best media campaign Ive ever seen. And it was made with the blood of women and girls. I've been in and around media for longer than I care to admit. And I'll be honest with you, most of what passes for "great creative" these days makes me want to lie down in a dark room. But every now and then..... Every now and then. Something lands on your desk, or in this case, my feed and you just... stop. Not because it's loud. Not because it's got some cracking bit of CGI or a celebrity doing something unexpected. But because it's so still that it almost feels rude. A newspaper page. A small blood stain. Barely anything else. And yet I haven't stopped thinking about it. Attention is something you buy. You spend enough, you shout loud enough, you optimise hard enough, and eventually people will care. They won't. You cannot buy the kind of attention this campaign earns. You can only get there by understanding something about human beings that no media plan will ever teach you: We don't remember what we're told. We remember what we figure out for ourselves. This campaign leaves a tiny gap between what you see and what you understand. Just enough space for your brain to lean in. To do the work. To complete the story. And the second you complete it, it's no longer their message. It's yours. And in 15 years of watching campaigns come and go, I can count on one hand the number of times I've seen it done properly. Now, this isn't a campaign flogging trainers or shifting units. This is for an issue that is genuinely, shamefully underserved. One that deserves a proper spotlight. And whoever sat in whatever room and decided that this was the way to do it, with restraint, with intelligence, with genuine respect for the audience's intelligence. Mate. Absolute hat tip to you. Because the temptation, always, always the temptation, is to do more. More copy. More explanation. More hand-holding. More desperate signposting because someone in a meeting got nervous and wanted to make sure everyone got it. The bravery here is in what they didn't do. There is a difference between advertising and art. Advertising interrupts thought. Art creates it. This is art. The most radical thing you can do is trust a brilliant idea to speak for itself. This one did. Whoever came up with it deserves a proper standing ovation. Not polite LinkedIn clapping. An actual one. This, ladies and gentlemen, is what we should all be trying to make. ...more ...more**
